$comment: Hand-curated from standard anatomy references (Moore's Clinically Oriented Anatomy, Gray's Anatomy). DRAFT: not yet reviewed by an anatomist. Report errors via the app.

axillary.name: Axillary nerve
axillary.lesion: Weak shoulder abduction beyond 15°, flattened shoulder contour, numb patch over the lateral upper arm (regimental badge area). Classic cause: fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus or shoulder dislocation.

musculocutaneous.name: Musculocutaneous nerve
musculocutaneous.lesion: Weak elbow flexion and supination; reduced biceps reflex; numb lateral forearm.

radial.name: Radial nerve
radial.lesion: Wrist drop: cannot extend the wrist or fingers at the knuckles; weak elbow extension if injured high in the arm. Classic cause: fracture of the humeral shaft (radial groove).

median.name: Median nerve
median.lesion: High injury: weak forearm pronation and flexion of the lateral fingers (hand of benediction on making a fist). At the wrist (carpal tunnel): weak thumb opposition, thenar wasting, numb lateral three and a half digits.

ulnar.name: Ulnar nerve
ulnar.lesion: Claw hand of the ring and little fingers, weak finger abduction and adduction, weak thumb adduction (Froment's sign), numb medial one and a half digits. Classic cause: injury at the medial epicondyle.

femoral.name: Femoral nerve
femoral.lesion: Weak knee extension and hip flexion, lost knee-jerk reflex, numb anterior thigh and medial leg.

obturator.name: Obturator nerve
obturator.lesion: Weak thigh adduction; the leg swings outward when walking; numb patch on the medial thigh.

superior_gluteal.name: Superior gluteal nerve
superior_gluteal.lesion: Weak hip abduction: positive Trendelenburg sign, the pelvis drops on the opposite side when standing on the affected leg.

inferior_gluteal.name: Inferior gluteal nerve
inferior_gluteal.lesion: Weak hip extension: difficulty rising from a chair or climbing stairs.

sciatic_tibial.name: Tibial nerve (sciatic, tibial part)
sciatic_tibial.lesion: Weak knee flexion (hamstrings), lost plantarflexion and toe flexion, cannot stand on tiptoe, numb sole.

common_fibular.name: Common fibular nerve
common_fibular.lesion: Foot drop: cannot dorsiflex or evert the foot, high-stepping gait, numb dorsum of the foot. Classic cause: injury at the neck of the fibula.
